key_insight: The paper shows that unified multimodal models can learn to “reflect” on their own image outputs and improve them through an interleaved reinforcement learning loop. The core breakthrough is jointly optimizing reflection text and image generation so the model learns which revisions actually lead to better final images.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of training multimodal models to self-correct image generations when the usefulness of a reflection can only be judged after the revised image is rendered. Standard supervised fine-tuning provides a weak starting point, but it does not reliably discover high-success repair trajectories.
method: Use supervised fine-tuning on reflection trajectories to provide a cold start for the model.
Train reflection and image generation together in an interleaved RL loop, where the model observes the rendered result and updates its diagnosis-and-repair strategy.
Optimize for successful self-repair paths rather than only imitation, enabling the model to learn native reflection behavior.
impact: This matters for practitioners building unified multimodal systems because it improves self-correction without requiring separate external critique models. It can lead to more reliable image generation workflows and more capable agentic multimodal models that learn from their own outputs.

paper_title: Learning Native Reflection in Unified Models with Interleaved Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Yijia Fan, Ziqi Huang, Zhongang Cai, Yan Li, Zimo Wen
